questions.q: Simplify: $12.6 \div 0.3 \times 0.5$
questions.solution: $\div$ and $\times$ have equal precedence, so work left to right: $12.6 \div 0.3 = 42$, then $42 \times 0.5 = 21$.
questions.shortcut: Never do $0.3 \times 0.5$ first — that gives the trap option 84. Left-to-right on equal precedence.

questions.q: What is the value of $7 + 77 + 777 + 7777 + 77777$?
questions.shortcut: Sum of repunits $1+11+111+1111+11111 = 12345$ — memorise; answer $= 7 \times 12345 = 86415$.

questions.q: In an election between two candidates, 85% of the 40,000 registered voters cast their votes and 5% of the votes polled were declared invalid. The winning candidate received 60% of the valid votes. How many valid votes did the winning candidate receive?
questions.shortcut: Chain the percentages on one line: $40000 \to \times 0.85 \to \times 0.95 \to \times 0.6 = 19380$.

questions.q: The population of City A is 25% more than the population of City B. City B's population is what per cent of City A's population?
questions.shortcut: A $=\frac{5}{4}$B $\Rightarrow$ B $= \frac{4}{5}$A $= 80\%$ of A (fraction table: $\frac{1}{5} = 20\%$).

questions.q: A starts a business with ₹36,000. After 4 months B joins with ₹48,000. At the end of the year the profit is ₹34,000. What is A's share of the profit?
questions.solution: Profit ratio $=$ capital $\times$ months: A $= 36000 \times 12 = 432000$, B $= 48000 \times 8 = 384000$, i.e. $9 : 8$. A's share $= \frac{9}{17} \times 34000 = ₹18{,}000$.
questions.shortcut: Reduce the capital-months to 9 : 8 immediately; A gets 9 parts of 17 — $34000/17 = 2000$ per part.

questions.q: The average weight of a group of 8 persons increases by 2.5 kg when a new person replaces one weighing 65 kg. The weight of the new person is:
questions.solution: Total increase $= 8 \times 2.5 = 20$ kg. New person $= 65 + 20 = 85$ kg.
questions.shortcut: Weight of replacement = outgoing weight $+$ (count $\times$ rise in average) $= 65 + 20 = 85$ kg.

questions.q: A sum of money becomes 3 times itself in 8 years at simple interest. In how many years will it become 7 times itself at the same rate?
questions.solution: Becoming 3 times means SI gained $= 2P$ in 8 years, so $1P$ of interest takes 4 years. To become 7 times it must gain $6P$, i.e. $6 \times 4 = 24$ years.
questions.shortcut: Only the gain counts: 2 units of interest in 8 yr → 1 unit per 4 yr → 6 units in 24 yr.

questions.q: A trader marks his article 60% above its cost price and allows a discount of 25%. If the article is sold for ₹14,400, what is its cost price?
questions.shortcut: Net factor $= 1.6 	imes 0.75 = 1.2$, so SP is 120% of CP: CP $= 14400 	imes  rac{100}{120} = 12000$.

questions.q: A man sells a watch at a loss of 10%. Had he sold it for ₹540 more, he would have gained 5%. The cost price of the watch is:
questions.solution: The ₹540 bridges a 10% loss and a 5% gain, so it equals $15\%$ of CP. CP $= \frac{540 \times 100}{15} = ₹3{,}600$.
questions.shortcut: Difference of the two scenarios $=$ (5 $-$ ($-$10))% of CP: CP $= \frac{540}{15}\% = 3600$.

questions.q: A can finish a piece of work in 20 days and B can finish it in 30 days. They work together for 6 days and then A leaves. In how many days will B alone finish the remaining work?
questions.solution: One-day rates: $\frac{1}{20} + \frac{1}{30} = \frac{1}{12}$. In 6 days they do $\frac{6}{12} = \frac{1}{2}$. Remaining $\frac{1}{2}$ at $\frac{1}{30}$ per day takes 15 days, so total $= 6 + 15 = 21$ days from the start.
questions.shortcut: LCM 60 units: A 3 u/day, B 2 u/day, 5 u/day; 6 days = 30 u done, 30 left for B at 2 u/day = 15 days.

questions.q: A train 240 m long crosses a platform 360 m long in 30 seconds. The speed of the train is:
questions.shortcut: Total length ÷ time, then $\times  rac{18}{5}$: $ rac{600}{30} \times  rac{18}{5} = 72$ km/h.

questions.q: If $x + \frac{1}{x} = 6$, what is the value of $x^3 + \frac{1}{x^3}$?
questions.shortcut: Cube-ladder: for $x+ rac1x = k$, the next rung is $k^3 - 3k = 216 - 18 = 198$.

questions.q: If $a + b + c = 9$ and $ab + bc + ca = 23$, what is the value of $a^3 + b^3 + c^3 - 3abc$?
questions.shortcut: Direct identity: $(s)(s^2 - 3p)$ with $s=9, p=23$ gives $9 \times 12 = 108$.

questions.q: In $\triangle ABC$, $AD$ is the bisector of $\angle A$ meeting $BC$ at $D$. If $AB = 8$ cm, $AC = 12$ cm and $BC = 15$ cm, what is the length of $BD$?
questions.solution: By the angle-bisector theorem $\frac{BD}{DC} = \frac{AB}{AC} = \frac{8}{12} = \frac{2}{3}$, so $BD = \frac{2}{5} \times 15 = 6$ cm.
questions.shortcut: Split $BC$ in ratio $2:3$ — 5 parts of 15 give 6 per part.

questions.q: A chord of length 30 cm is at a distance of 8 cm from the centre of a circle. The radius of the circle is:
questions.shortcut: 8-15-17 triplet: radius is the hypotenuse of half-chord and distance.

questions.q: From an external point $P$, a tangent $PT = 15$ cm and a secant $PAB$ are drawn to a circle. If $PA = 9$ cm ($A$ nearer to $P$), what is the length of the chord $AB$?
questions.solution: $PT^2 = PA \cdot PB \Rightarrow PB = \frac{15^2}{9} = 25$ cm. $AB = PB - PA = 25 - 9 = 16$ cm.
questions.shortcut: $\frac{225}{9} = 25$ = full secant; subtract the external part 9.

questions.q: The angle of elevation of the top of a tower from a point on the ground is $30^\circ$. On walking 30 m directly towards its base, the angle of elevation becomes $45^\circ$. The height of the tower is:
questions.solution: Let the height be $h$ and the near point be $h$ m from the base ($45^\circ$). Then the far point is at $h\sqrt{3}$, so $h\sqrt{3} - h = 30 \Rightarrow h = \frac{30}{\sqrt{3}-1} = 15(\sqrt{3}+1)$ m.
questions.shortcut: With angles $30^\circ \to 45^\circ$: extra distance $= h(\sqrt{3}-1)$, so $h = \frac{30}{\sqrt{3}-1} = 15(\sqrt{3}+1)$.

questions.q: The diagonals of a rhombus are 24 cm and 10 cm. The perimeter of the rhombus is:
questions.solution: Diagonals bisect at right angles, so side $= \sqrt{12^2 + 5^2} = 13$ cm. Perimeter $= 4 \times 13 = 52$ cm.
questions.shortcut: 5-12-13 triplet — side 13, perimeter 52.

questions.q: The total surface area of a solid cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 20 cm is: [Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$]
If $3\tan\theta = 4$ and $\theta$ is acute, what is the value of $\frac{4\sin\theta - 2\cos\theta}{4\sin\theta + 2\cos\theta}$?
questions.shortcut: Divide the whole expression by $\cos\theta$ and put $\tan = \frac{4}{3}$: $\frac{4\tan - 2}{4\tan + 2} = \frac{16-6}{16+6} = \frac{5}{11}$.

questions.q: If $\sin\theta + \text{cosec}\,\theta = 5$, what is the value of $\sin^2\theta + \text{cosec}^2\theta$?
questions.solution: Square both sides: $\sin^2\theta + \text{cosec}^2\theta + 2 = 25$, so the value $= 25 - 2 = 23$.
questions.shortcut: Sum-with-reciprocal: square and subtract 2.

questions.q: What is the median of the first six prime numbers?
questions.shortcut: Even count → average the 3rd and 4th values: $(5+7)/2 = 6$.

questions.q:
The table shows the number of smartphones sold by four stores P, Q, R and S in three months:

| Store | January | February | March |
|---|---|---|---|
| P | 320 | 280 | 400 |
| Q | 240 | 360 | 300 |
| R | 400 | 320 | 240 |
| S | 280 | 240 | 360 |

What is the ratio of the total sales of store P to the total sales of store S over the three months?
questions.shortcut: Both totals end in 0 — divide by 40 first: $25:22$.

questions.q:
The table shows the number of smartphones sold by four stores P, Q, R and S in three months:

| Store | January | February | March |
|---|---|---|---|
| P | 320 | 280 | 400 |
| Q | 240 | 360 | 300 |
| R | 400 | 320 | 240 |
| S | 280 | 240 | 360 |

The sales of store Q in February are what per cent of the total sales of all four stores in February?
questions.shortcut: $360/1200 = 3/10 = 30\%$ straight from the fraction table.

questions.q:
The table shows the number of smartphones sold by four stores P, Q, R and S in three months:

| Store | January | February | March |
|---|---|---|---|
| P | 320 | 280 | 400 |
| Q | 240 | 360 | 300 |
| R | 400 | 320 | 240 |
| S | 280 | 240 | 360 |

What is the average monthly sale of store R over the three months?
questions.shortcut: Units digit trick: $960/3 = 320$; totals of 9 are divisible by 3.
